documents.text: ## `eslint:recommended` changes Two new rules have been added to the [`eslint:recommended`](configure/configuration-files#use-predefined-configurations) config: - [`no-compare-neg-zero`](../rules/no-compare-neg-zero) disallows comparisons to `-0` - [`no-useless-escape`](../rules/no-useless-escape) disallows uselessly-escaped characters in strings and regular expressions **To address:** To mimic the `eslint:recommended` behavior from 3.x, you can disable these rules in a config file: ```json { "extends": "eslint:recommended", "rules": { "no-compare-neg-zero": "off", "no-useless-escape": "off" } } ```

## <a name="eslint-recommended-changes"/> `eslint:recommended` changes

Two new rules have been added to the [`eslint:recommended`](configure/configuration-files#use-predefined-configurations) config:

- [`for-direction`](../rules/for-direction) enforces that a `for` loop update clause moves the counter in the right direction.
- [`getter-return`](../rules/getter-return) enforces that a `return` statement is present in property getters.

**To address:** To mimic the `eslint:recommended` behavior from 4.x, you can disable these rules in a config file:

```json
{
	"extends": "eslint:recommended",

	"rules": {
		"for-direction": "off",
		"getter-return": "off"
	}
}
```

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
